title: Large personal ST/Amiga/DOS game and application restoration discovery
summary: Personally screen 691 candidate URLs and add 20 projects, with four explicit non-promotion decisions.
notes: Root assistant personally searched 16 GitHub query routes across Amiga, Atari ST, CPC and DOS plus retained leads, screened 691 unique URLs and reviewed 24 repositories. Twenty additions and four explicit non-promotions. Distinguish original-source restoration, native behavioral ports, compiler-matching reconstruction, source-derived format converters and code/clock emulation. Cavequest uses six-byte normalization; DemoVT copies the packer stub/header; Scorched Earth compares to a Python oracle, not original execution. No new CPC engine was invented to fill a quota. No upstream game, compiler, installer, extender, modem or emulator was executed.

sources.reason: GOG 1.21 reconstruction with 1.12/PS1/Rayverse semantic references; inspected Blacktoon logic and status separation.
Reverse-engineered legacy LeScript document reader producing HTML; inspected control-code handling and explicit lossy conversions.
GOS4/GOS5 launcher reconstruction and native 68k file-service patches for GEMDOS/GEMDRIVE hard-disk game adaptations; inspected original-byte source mapping description and GOS4 patch.
Three DOS adventure executables reconstructed into address-linked choice/parser datasets and a browser reference engine; command comparisons, aliases and destinations retained.
Native Go rules, state and BBS interface recovered from the DOS 3.6 distribution and captured behavior. Inspected transactional combat logic with recovered duel semantics.
Original VGA/LVL formats recovered and loaded by native C engine; inspected asset-loader validation. The author explicitly distinguishes this from decompilation.
Recovered game routines and resource data expressed as native C++ state, physics and rendering; inspected original-address-linked projectile/terrain logic.
Historical simulator/replay of ToneLoc screens, result codes and DAT format ported from the released 1994 C source; inspected typed Rust parser.
Recovered QUEST.COM/QUEST.000 source and structured combat includes. Inspected post-build normalizer as well as implementation.
Recovered ELEPS game in procedural Turbo Pascal; inspected records, state and game routines. Upstream reports exact LZEXE-packed output and ordered relocation matches.
Original 1992 function-grapher Pascal units preserved alongside native JavaScript parser/differentiator and plotting UI. Inspected matching operator structure in FUNC.PAS and mathEngine.js.
Recovered 1999 text RPG and units, with original-author-approved lineage from rzuf79/bombki. Inspected MONSTRA Pascal unit and TP7 conformance requirements.
Original 1989-94 menu-system sources recovered from backups, with v1 and rewritten v3 histories preserved; inspected original desktop/window object code.
Recovered N-body simulator plus HELP and KLOK programs with original-offset C++ source and QuickBASIC-compatible error/runtime behavior.
1998-99 extender source modernized for NASM/Open Watcom/UPX with native LE/PE/RDOFF loaders and DPMI host; inspected original-attributed LE loader.
JavaScript compiler emits genuine 68k HUNK/ADF output; reverse-engineered EMOD/OOP ABI supports original binary modules. Inspected module reader and original-compiler comparison documentation.
Five games have separate maintained C/assembly decompilation trees plus native SDL3 ports; inspected CM1 source and matching guide, not just instruction-translated recompiler output.
Source-controlled continuation of K1n9_Duk3 recovered game code with actual original-attributed level/game modules; original author/reconstructor credits retained.
Recovered DemoVT 1.31b/1.51 music players with documented generated-clean source; inspected 1.51 S3M loader. This is the player application/subsystem, not the separately scoped Psycho Neurosis demo.
Native TS physics/game/renderer derived from the authors Python reconstruction; inspected address-linked projectile formulas and explicit oracle boundary.

Primarily instruction-by-instruction C translation retaining registers/clocks and an emulated PC, with incremental named replacements. Preserve for architecture audit rather than call the full game a recovered high-level native engine.
README explicitly says original resident DOS memory image runs under Unicorn CPU/hardware emulation. SAPI wrapper is not recovered speech-engine source.
Modern from-scratch Oberon-07 DOS compiler, not reconstruction of a historical compiler/application. Relevant modern retro tooling can be reviewed separately.

Original personal GW-BASIC archive decoded with PC-BASIC and presented through an emulator, not binary-derived application reconstruction. Keep archival lead separately; do not ingest unrelated family details.

decisions.title: Svinjoland trilogy — recovered adventure models and browser engine
decisions.reason: Three DOS adventure executables reconstructed into address-linked choice/parser datasets and a browser reference engine; command comparisons, aliases and destinations retained.

decisions.title: Yankee Trader: Resurrection — Go BBS game reconstruction
decisions.reason: Native Go rules, state and BBS interface recovered from the DOS 3.6 distribution and captured behavior. Inspected transactional combat logic with recovered duel semantics.

decisions.title: Magic Mushroom — C/SDL2 format-derived recreation
decisions.reason: Original VGA/LVL formats recovered and loaded by native C engine; inspected asset-loader validation. The author explicitly distinguishes this from decompilation.

decisions.title: Karnov DOS — native Windows reconstruction
decisions.reason: Recovered game routines and resource data expressed as native C++ state, physics and rendering; inspected original-address-linked projectile/terrain logic.

decisions.title: ToneLoc — Rust archive-format and interface reconstruction
decisions.reason: Historical simulator/replay of ToneLoc screens, result codes and DAT format ported from the released 1994 C source; inspected typed Rust parser.

decisions.title: Cavequest 1.1 — Turbo Pascal source reconstruction
decisions.reason: Recovered QUEST.COM/QUEST.000 source and structured combat includes. Inspected post-build normalizer as well as implementation.

decisions.title: Arabela 1.06 — packed Pascal matching reconstruction
decisions.reason: Recovered ELEPS game in procedural Turbo Pascal; inspected records, state and game routines. Upstream reports exact LZEXE-packed output and ordered relocation matches.

decisions.title: ISGRAF — original Pascal grapher and JavaScript restoration
decisions.reason: Original 1992 function-grapher Pascal units preserved alongside native JavaScript parser/differentiator and plotting UI. Inspected matching operator structure in FUNC.PAS and mathEngine.js.

decisions.title: BOMBKI — Pascal matching recovery and native ports
decisions.reason: Recovered 1999 text RPG and units, with original-author-approved lineage from rzuf79/bombki. Inspected MONSTRA Pascal unit and TP7 conformance requirements.

decisions.title: Power-Choice — recovered original DOS menu-system source
decisions.reason: Original 1989-94 menu-system sources recovered from backups, with v1 and rewritten v3 histories preserved; inspected original desktop/window object code.

decisions.title: GRAVITY — QuickBASIC simulator recovered in C++
decisions.reason: Recovered N-body simulator plus HELP and KLOK programs with original-offset C++ source and QuickBASIC-compatible error/runtime behavior.

decisions.title: ZRDX — restored Zurenava DOS extender
decisions.reason: 1998-99 extender source modernized for NASM/Open Watcom/UPX with native LE/PE/RDOFF loaders and DPMI host; inspected original-attributed LE loader.

decisions.title: ecomp — Amiga E compiler/interface reconstruction
decisions.reason: JavaScript compiler emits genuine 68k HUNK/ADF output; reverse-engineered EMOD/OOP ABI supports original binary modules. Inspected module reader and original-compiler comparison documentation.

decisions.title: Championship Manager DOS series — matching source and native ports
decisions.reason: Five games have separate maintained C/assembly decompilation trees plus native SDL3 ports; inspected CM1 source and matching guide, not just instruction-translated recompiler output.

decisions.title: Hocus Pocus — K1n9_Duk3 reconstruction continuation
decisions.reason: Source-controlled continuation of K1n9_Duk3 recovered game code with actual original-attributed level/game modules; original author/reconstructor credits retained.

decisions.title: DemoVT — Pascal music-player matching reconstructions
decisions.reason: Recovered DemoVT 1.31b/1.51 music players with documented generated-clean source; inspected 1.51 S3M loader. This is the player application/subsystem, not the separately scoped Psycho Neurosis demo.

decisions.title: Scorched Earth — TypeScript source-derived browser port
decisions.reason: Native TS physics/game/renderer derived from the authors Python reconstruction; inspected address-linked projectile formulas and explicit oracle boundary.

decisions.title: TideGear/OpenNighthawk
decisions.reason: Primarily instruction-by-instruction C translation retaining registers/clocks and an emulated PC, with incremental named replacements. Preserve for architecture audit rather than call the full game a recovered high-level native engine.

decisions.title: joshknnd1982/smoothtalker-sapi5
decisions.reason: README explicitly says original resident DOS memory image runs under Unicorn CPU/hardware emulation. SAPI wrapper is not recovered speech-engine source.

decisions.title: DosWorld/toc
decisions.reason: Modern from-scratch Oberon-07 DOS compiler, not reconstruction of a historical compiler/application. Relevant modern retro tooling can be reviewed separately.

decisions.title: jakiestfu/sams-calendar-program
decisions.reason: Original personal GW-BASIC archive decoded with PC-BASIC and presented through an emulator, not binary-derived application reconstruction. Keep archival lead separately; do not ingest unrelated family details.
